summary: A dense worker-placement game where you send unique worker types (each with escalating strength-based bonuses) to build outposts, commission monks for combos, or confront raiders, while managing a hidden virtue/corruption track that shapes which endgame bonuses you can claim. It's slower and more of a brain-burner than its siblings Architects and Merchants, rewarding a coherent long-term engine over reactive play.
praised: Strong thematic and mechanical variety within one system (building, faith, combat)
Satisfying engine-building via monk commissioning combos
Meaningful choices around the virtue/corruption alignment track
criticised: Heaviest and most fiddly of the West Kingdom trilogy, with a steeper learning curve
Can feel a bit dry or spreadsheet-like compared to Architects
Significant downtime in higher player counts
Some randomness in the market/outsider decks can swing outcomes
Rulebook and icon-heavy components require a learning investment

interaction.kind: worker placement blocking and spot competition

scoring.why: Points come from a mix of outposts, fortifications, commissioned monks, confronted outsiders, and endgame bonuses tied to virtue/strength/influence tracks.
